step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 20-month-old female child undergoing dental crown restoration of a malformed incisor

step5_concept_grounding: Congenital Zika virus syndrome (ZVCS) as historical baseline comorbidity in dental restoration case

evidence_items.source_quote: A 20-month-old female patient with ZVCS presented with her mother at the School of Dentistry Clinic with a chief complaint of self-injury in both hands secondary to a "pointed tooth" (Figures 1A and 1B).

rationale: A 20-month-old female presenting to a pediatric dental clinic for CAD/CAM restoration of a pointed deciduous incisor. Although noted to have congenital Zika virus syndrome with microcephaly and arthrogryposis, no diagnostic laboratory confirmation (PCR or serology) is reported in the case narrative. The primary subject of the report is restorative dental technique, and Zika is a historical congenital background comorbidity without active infection or E1/E2 evidence in the current episode. Excluded as non-target case.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Male in his 60s presenting with bilateral peripheral facial nerve paralysis and GBS

step5_concept_grounding: Evaluation of suspected acute Zika virus infection in patient with GBS

evidence_items.source_quote: ZIKV qRT-PCR was performed locally on urine taken at day four after admission and was negative.

rationale: A male in his 60s presenting with bilateral peripheral facial nerve palsy and Guillain-Barré syndrome during a Zika outbreak in Suriname. Local real-time RT-PCR on urine was negative for ZIKV (E0 non-confirmatory/refuting evidence). No active confirmed Zika infection was documented in the clinical case presentation. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 10-month-old infant monitored for potential transmission after consuming Zika-positive breast milk

step5_concept_grounding: Surveillance and laboratory exclusion of Zika virus transmission in breastfed infant

evidence_items.source_quote: The child's urine samples were negative for ZIKV RT-PCR (collected 7 times between December 12, 2017 and January 5, 2018) despite ingesting breast milk with detectable ZIKV RNA. Blood samples for Zika IgG and IgM serology testing on January 5 and 30, 2018 were negative.

rationale: A 10-month-old infant monitored following daily ingestion of breast milk containing ZIKV RNA from an infected mother. Serial urine RT-PCR tests (collected 7 times) and serum IgM/IgG serology were negative (E0 refuting evidence), definitively confirming lack of transmission. Assigned NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 3-year-old girl presenting with tracheoinnominate fistula following tracheostomy

step5_concept_grounding: Chronic baseline neurological condition (Zika syndrome) noted in surgical vascular case

evidence_items.source_quote: A three-year-old bed-ridden girl presenting a chronic neurologic condition (Zika syndrome) was admitted to treat an episode of tracheitis.

rationale: A 3-year-old girl presenting with a massive tracheoinnominate fistula bleeding episode successfully managed by endovascular stenting. While noted to have a chronic neurological background condition described as Zika syndrome, no active diagnostic workup or confirmatory testing for Zika was performed. The primary diagnosis is tracheoinnominate fistula. Excluded as non-target case.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Ethics statement / study preamble referring to a rare Zika case reported in full in subsequent section

step5_concept_grounding: Introductory statement and ethics approval mention of a Zika case

evidence_items.source_quote: Based on the above considerations, here we investigated a rare Zika case, in which an infected 28-year-old pregnant patient was diagnosed with GBS and had a spontaneous abortion.

rationale: This text snippet represents only the introductory sentence and ethics approval of the study, lacking clinical case presentation, diagnostic timeline, or laboratory findings. The clinical narrative is reported in PMC5964188_02. Excluded as non-case report snippet.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: 3-year-old male child with morning glory disc anomaly following maternal gestational Zika exposure

step5_concept_grounding: Maternal gestational Zika virus exposure evaluated in child with congenital optic disc anomaly

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to her symptoms, the mother underwent a real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test for ZIKV with positive results.

rationale: A 3-year-old male presenting with morning glory disc anomaly (MGDA) and strabismus. Perinatal history notes that the mother tested positive by RT-PCR for ZIKV during pregnancy. However, the patient himself was not tested or confirmed to have had Zika virus infection, and maternal gestational exposure serves only as epidemiological background. The primary case focus is an ophthalmologic malformation. Excluded as non-target case.
